title: TokenizeResponse
description: The answer to POST /tokenize. Every offset is a UTF-16 code unit offset into its block's text. Every token is returned, so a block's tokens cover its text in order with no gap and no overlap, and a token with no word has w null.

version.description: The tokenizer's version, the word rules, the lexicon's version and the sidecar's, joined by ';', as in sudachipy=0.6.11;sudachidict_full=20260723;modes=C/A;words=6;lexicon=<version>;sidecar=3. The lexicon's version holds ';' too, so compare the whole string. A change in any part can change the tokens of the same text.

words.description: The words the blocks use, each once across the whole response, keyed by lemma, pos and isProper. A token's w is an index into this list.

blocks.description: One entry per request block, in request order.

phrases.description: The block's phrases in text order, never overlapping, possibly none. A phrase lies over the tokens and changes none of them.

blind.description: The s of each top-level token whose reading the sentence couldn't have changed, in text order, possibly none. Sudachi's dictionary has other entries with the token's surface, dictionary form, part of speech and connection ids that read it differently, so its fixed costs alone picked the reading, as with 瞬く read しばたたく. A rival counts only when it reads one of the word's offered entries that isn't all affix or counter senses (suf, pref, ctr, n-suf, n-pref), so 顔's suffix がお doesn't make 顔 blind. When an offered entry with the token's own reading is common, the rival's entry must be common and so must the rival's own kana form there, so 男 read おとこ isn't blind for the rare おのこ, nor 女性 じょせい for にょしょう, while 瞬く read しばたたく, whose entry isn't common, weighs every rival. Readings that one JMdict entry gives the same senses don't count, and a joined unit is never blind.

wordIndex.description: An index into words, or null for particles, symbols, numbers, counters, whitespace and long units the lexicon doesn't know.

reading.description: The hiragana reading of this occurrence, or null when its text has no kanji. When Sudachi's reading is a kana form of exactly one offered entry, and the entry's first reading takes the same senses, it is that first reading, so 言っ reads いっ where Sudachi gave ゆっ.

subToken.description: [s, e, w, r] for one short-unit part of a long unit.

phrase.description: [s, e, w] for a JMdict expression that spans 2 to 6 tokens with a particle or a verb inside, such as 気がする over 気+が+し. s and e fall on token boundaries, and w is an index into words, a word with pos 表現.

token.description: [s, e, w, r, sub]. sub is null, or the short-unit parts when the long unit splits and the unit or one of its parts has a word. When w is null and sub isn't, the words are in the parts. Neighbouring Sudachi tokens that spell a JMdict headword come back joined as one such long unit, 神様 with the parts 神 and 様, and a joined unit's parts are the tokens it joined, never their own parts.

seq.description: The JMdict seq, the part of a sense key before the colon.

common.description: For a lemma with a kanji, the kanji form it is spelled with is common in the entry and so is one of readings. For a kana lemma, its kana form is common in the entry.

readings.description: The entry's kana forms that read this spelling, in hiragana and JMdict's order. A form whose appliesToKanji leaves the spelling out is not here, nor a search-only (sk) form, nor an outdated, irregular or rare one (ok, ik, rk) unless the entry has nothing else. A kana lemma reads as itself.

lemma.description: The dictionary form when it is all kana, otherwise Sudachi's normalized form.

pos.description: The first level of Sudachi's part of speech, such as 名詞 or 動詞, or 表現 for a phrase's word.

isProper.description: Sudachi tags the token 固有名詞. A name and a common word written the same are two words.

reading.description: The lemma's reading in hiragana, the same for every occurrence. It comes from the entries that match Sudachi's reading of the lemma, as shimen's own word rows do, and is the first of the first such entry's entries readings.

jlpt.description: The JLPT level from 5 (easiest) to 1, or null, from the same entries as reading.

readings.description: The word's reading, then the other hiragana kana forms of the offered entries, entry by entry in the order senses gives them. For a lemma with a kanji the offered entries are every JMdict entry written with the lemma (or with the dictionary form when the lemma has none), so a heteronym such as 辛い offers both からい and つらい. For a kana lemma they are the entries that match its reading. Empty when no entry matched.

senses.description: The senses of the offered entries. The entries that match Sudachi's reading come first, in the lexicon's order, then the others written with the lemma, common ones first, then by seq. Within an entry, senses follow JMdict's order. A sense JMdict restricts to other spellings, or to readings this spelling lacks, is left out.

key.description: <JMdict seq>:<n>, n counted from 1 within the entry, the key shimen's annotations use.

r.description: Present only when JMdict restricts the sense to some of the readings of its entry: those readings, in hiragana. It is left out when the sense takes every reading in its entry's readings, and it can name a reading that readings leaves out as outdated.

entries.description: One item per offered JMdict entry, in the order their senses come in senses.
